sn35.127:1.1: Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer declares enlightenment at [sn48.49](), resulting in him being praised as the foremost in roaring a lion’s roar ([an1.195]()). He was noted for his austere lifestyle ([ud4.6]()), which he explained in his verses at [thag2.2](). He and Moggallāna once egged each other on to win a psychic power contest, for which he was reprimanded by the Buddha ([pli-tv-kd15:8.1.1]()).
sn35.127:1.2: Udena of Kosambī features in [ud7.1](), a key event in the so-called “Kosambī cycle”.
sn35.127:1.5: Despite the claim here, this saying is not spoken by the Buddha in the Pali. Perhaps the original discourse was lost.
sn35.127:1.6: A healthy monastic life cannot be lived in fear and loathing of the opposite sex. A positive emotional connection is grounded in _mettā_, derived ultimately from the experience of familial love, just as a mother’s cherishing of her child is the basis for universal love ([snp1.8:7.1]()).
sn35.127:3.2: The perception of kindness, cherishing, and love is established regarding the opposite sex, while detachment is cultivated for one’s own body.
sn35.127:5.3: With _esova_ (“this is the real”), the king shows that he was unpersuaded by the other practices, but is convinced by this one, which agrees with his experience.
sn35.127:5.4: The _antepura_ is the “inner sanctum”, sometimes the enclosed area of the “royal compound” ([dn14:2.2.10]()), but here the women’s apartments or “harem”.
